raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible as an elevation-transect ensemble of single-column ELM runs; each column is 1-D and vertically resolved but laterally decoupled.",
    "answerable": [
      "Column-level water balance partitioning (precip into snow/rain, ET components, surface runoff, subsurface drainage, snowmelt, soil-moisture storage) as a function of elevation",
      "Elevation-dependent snowpack accumulation/ablation timing and SWE",
      "Elevation gradients in evapotranspiration and its partitioning (transpiration/soil evap/canopy evap)",
      "Relative contribution of snowmelt vs rainfall to runoff generation along the transect"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Lateral hydrologic routing or river discharge at the basin outlet (single-column ELM has no lateral connectivity/streamflow routing)",
      "Groundwater flow between columns or hillslope-scale redistribution",
      "Glacier dynamics/ice-melt contribution (ELM lacks a dynamic glacier hydrology model)",
      "Sub-grid catchment-integrated water yield without an external routing model (e.g., MOSART)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "Five columns span the Bow River headwaters elevation gradient from the montane valley floor (~1400 m) to the alpine zone (~2600 m), capturing the transition in snow-vs-rain partitioning, ET, and runoff timing that drives elevation-resolved water partitioning while keeping the ensemble computationally tractable.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "bow_valley_canmore_1400m", "lat": 51.089, "lon": -115.359, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "bow_lake_louise_1540m", "lat": 51.425, "lon": -116.182, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "bow_lake_2060m", "lat": 51.667, "lon": -116.454, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "bow_subalpine_2350m", "lat": 51.700, "lon": -116.500, "soil_texture": "gravelly_loam"},
    {"id": "bow_alpine_2600m", "lat": 51.720, "lon": -116.520, "soil_texture": "loamy_sand"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1991",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2010",
    "STOP_N": "20",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1991-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "RAIN", "SNOW", "H2OSNO", "SNOWDP", "FSNO", "QSNOMELT",
      "QRUNOFF", "QOVER", "QDRAI", "QINFL", "QCHARGE",
      "QVEGT", "QVEGE", "QSOIL", "EFLX_LH_TOT", "FCEV", "FCTR", "FGEV",
      "SOILLIQ", "SOILICE", "H2OSOI", "ZWT", "TWS",
      "RH2M", "TSA", "FSDS", "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": ["single_point_ELM", "GSWP3_or_CRUNCEP_forcing", "vertical_soil_hydrology", "snow_physics"],
  "assumptions": [
    "Atmospheric forcing (GSWP3/CRUNCEP) is elevation-corrected via lapse-rate downscaling of temperature, precipitation phase, and longwave to each column's true elevation",
    "20-year spin-up (accelerated decomposition then final steady-state) precedes the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snow states",
    "PFTs assigned per elevation: montane needleleaf evergreen forest at low sites, subalpine/krummholz at mid-high, alpine C3 grass/bare at highest column",
    "No glacier or lateral routing; results represent point/column water partitioning, not integrated basin discharge",
    "Surface datasets (soil texture, organic matter) derived from SoilGrids/default ELM surface data at each lat/lon",
    "Analysis reports multi-year mean seasonal water-budget partitioning across the transect"
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as an elevation-transect ensemble of single-column ELM runs; each column is 1-D and vertically resolved but laterally decoupled.
answerable: Column-level water balance partitioning (precip into snow/rain, ET components, surface runoff, subsurface drainage, snowmelt, soil-moisture storage) as a function of elevation
Elevation-dependent snowpack accumulation/ablation timing and SWE
Elevation gradients in evapotranspiration and its partitioning (transpiration/soil evap/canopy evap)
Relative contribution of snowmelt vs rainfall to runoff generation along the transect
not_answerable: Lateral hydrologic routing or river discharge at the basin outlet (single-column ELM has no lateral connectivity/streamflow routing)
Groundwater flow between columns or hillslope-scale redistribution
Glacier dynamics/ice-melt contribution (ELM lacks a dynamic glacier hydrology model)
Sub-grid catchment-integrated water yield without an external routing model (e.g., MOSART)

parsed.n_justification: Five columns span the Bow River headwaters elevation gradient from the montane valley floor (~1400 m) to the alpine zone (~2600 m), capturing the transition in snow-vs-rain partitioning, ET, and runoff timing that drives elevation-resolved water partitioning while keeping the ensemble computationally tractable.
assumptions: Atmospheric forcing (GSWP3/CRUNCEP) is elevation-corrected via lapse-rate downscaling of temperature, precipitation phase, and longwave to each column's true elevation
20-year spin-up (accelerated decomposition then final steady-state) precedes the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snow states
PFTs assigned per elevation: montane needleleaf evergreen forest at low sites, subalpine/krummholz at mid-high, alpine C3 grass/bare at highest column
No glacier or lateral routing; results represent point/column water partitioning, not integrated basin discharge
Surface datasets (soil texture, organic matter) derived from SoilGrids/default ELM surface data at each lat/lon
Analysis reports multi-year mean seasonal water-budget partitioning across the transect
